seo.title: Sciorex for Researchers - AI-Powered Research Environment | LaTeX, PDF Annotations, Reference Library
seo.description: A unified desktop environment for researchers: LaTeX editor with live preview, PDF annotation, AI-powered literature discovery, reference library, 3D molecule viewer, VS Code integration, and 59 MCP tools for autonomous research workflows. 100% local and free.

titleBlock.title: SCIOREX
titleBlock.subtitle: A Unified Environment for Research-Driven Software Development
titleBlock.abstract: We present Sciorex, an integrated desktop environment that unifies AI-assisted coding, visual workflow automation, and academic research tools into a single privacy-first application. Unlike existing solutions that force researchers to juggle multiple disconnected tools, Sciorex provides a seamless workspace where LaTeX editing, PDF annotation, literature discovery, AI-powered development, and project management coexist natively. Through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) layer exposing 59 custom tools, AI models can autonomously annotate PDFs, manage reference libraries, compile LaTeX documents, create and track tickets, and execute automation workflows—all while the researcher maintains full oversight and control. All computation and data storage occur locally on the user’s machine, ensuring complete data sovereignty.
titleBlock.keywords: research tools, AI coding, workflow automation, LaTeX, MCP protocol, desktop application, privacy-first, literature management, PDF annotation, 3D molecule viewer, VS Code, council mode, custom personas

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.p1: The modern research workflow is fractured across an ever-growing constellation of specialized tools. A computational researcher may begin their morning in a LaTeX editor, switch to a Jupyter notebook for exploratory analysis, consult a reference manager for literature review, open a separate PDF reader for annotation, use a terminal for version control, and finally context-switch into a project management tool to update collaborators. Each transition imposes a cognitive tax that compounds throughout the day {{cite3}}.
introduction.p2: Recent advances in large language models have introduced a new dimension to this problem. AI coding assistants {{cite1}} have demonstrated remarkable capability in accelerating software development, yet they exist as standalone applications or browser extensions—yet another window demanding the researcher’s fragmented attention. More critically, these AI assistants cannot interact with the researcher’s tools: they cannot annotate a PDF the researcher is reading, add a paper to the reference library, or create a ticket for a bug they discovered during code review.
introduction.p3: Sciorex addresses this fragmentation by providing a single, cohesive desktop environment purpose-built for researchers who write code. Drawing on principles from literate programming {{cite2}} and Bret Victor’s vision of immediate-feedback creative tools {{cite4}}, Sciorex integrates a LaTeX editor with live preview, a PDF annotation system, an AI-powered literature discovery engine, a multi-model chat interface, visual workflow automation, and full project management—all within a single window. Through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) layer {{cite5}}, these tools are not merely colocated but deeply interconnected: AI models can autonomously operate across every subsystem, transforming them from passive tools into active research collaborators.

research.title: Research Capabilities
research.intro: This section details the primary research-oriented features of Sciorex. These capabilities are designed to serve the daily needs of academic researchers, graduate students, and anyone whose work exists at the intersection of writing, reading, and programming.

latex.title: LaTeX Editing
latex.p1: Sciorex includes a fully integrated LaTeX editor with real-time PDF preview. The editor supports syntax highlighting, auto-completion of common LaTeX commands, multi-file project structures, and BibTeX integration. SyncTeX bidirectional navigation allows clicking on any position in the PDF to jump to the corresponding source line, and vice versa—eliminating the tedious process of manually locating source-preview correspondences. Over 30 publication-ready templates are included (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, IEEE, ACM, Nature, Springer, AAAI, PhD Thesis, and more), allowing researchers to begin writing in the correct format immediately. The LaTeX compilation toolchain runs locally with support for pdflatex, xelatex, and lualatex engines, and AI models can invoke it directly through MCP tools—compiling documents, inserting citations, and scaffolding standard structures (figures, tables, algorithms) on the researcher’s behalf.

pdf.title: PDF Annotation & Management
pdf.p1: Researchers spend a significant portion of their time reading and annotating papers. Sciorex provides a built-in PDF viewer with highlighting, freeform annotation, and structured note-taking. All annotations are stored locally and can be exported in standard formats. The annotation layer integrates with the reference library, allowing users to jump directly from a citation to the annotated source document. Crucially, the PDF tools are also exposed to AI models via MCP: an LLM can read a PDF, add highlights and margin notes, and retrieve existing annotations—enabling workflows like “summarize this paper and highlight the key findings.”

discovery.title: Literature Discovery
discovery.p1: Finding relevant papers is one of the most time-consuming aspects of research. Sciorex integrates an AI-powered literature discovery engine that allows researchers to search across 14 sources including Semantic Scholar, arXiv, CrossRef, PubMed, DBLP, OpenLibrary, Google Books, and Unpaywall. Beyond keyword search, the system offers a citation network explorer that visualizes the relationship between papers, enabling researchers to trace intellectual lineage and discover foundational works through graph traversal. The AI library tools allow models to search for papers, add them to the library, and organize them into collections—automating the literature survey process.

library.title: Reference Library
library.p1: All discovered and imported papers are organized in a local reference library that supports 43 distinct item types (journal articles, conference papers, books, theses, datasets, software, patents, and more) with 11 citation styles (APA 7th, MLA 9th, Chicago, IEEE, Harvard, Vancouver, Nature, Science, ACM, APS, and custom CSL) and 5 import/export formats (BibTeX, RIS, CSL-JSON, Zotero, and Mendeley). The library features collections, tags, full-text search, reading status tracking, and automatic metadata extraction from DOIs and arXiv identifiers. References can be directly inserted into LaTeX documents, and BibTeX entries are automatically generated and maintained. Through MCP, AI models have full access to the library: they can add items, update metadata, manage collections and tags, attach notes to papers, and link library items to project tickets—creating a fully connected research knowledge graph.

development.title: Development Environment
development.intro: While the research capabilities form the intellectual core of Sciorex, the development environment ensures that researchers who write code can do so without leaving the application. The following subsections describe the programming and automation tools available.

ai.title: AI-Assisted Coding
ai.p1: Sciorex includes built-in AI assistants that let you converse with leading AI models—Claude by Anthropic, Gemini by Google, GPT by OpenAI, or fully private local models that run on your own machine with no internet required. Under the hood, Sciorex orchestrates lightweight programs called AI CLIs (such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, LM Studio, and Ollama) that communicate directly with AI providers—Sciorex never proxies or stores conversations on intermediate servers. What matters for the researcher is what the AI can do: it can annotate your PDFs, manage your reference library, compile your LaTeX documents, create and track tickets, and execute automation workflows—all from a single conversation. The chat supports multiple modes: standard chat for general questions, an agentic mode where the AI can read, write, and edit files with the researcher reviewing each change, and a preview mode that opens a live browser panel. Extended Thinking levels (Think, Think Hard, Think Harder, Ultrathink) allow researchers to control the depth of AI reasoning for complex problems. A message queue system lets users continue composing follow-up instructions while the AI processes the current request, and context mentions (@file, @library, @ticket, @epic) inject relevant context directly into the conversation. Session forking allows branching a conversation at any point to explore alternative approaches without losing the original thread, and Select & Ask AI lets researchers highlight any text in the editor to instantly query the AI about it.

council.title: Council Mode
council.p1: For particularly complex problems—architectural decisions, debugging subtle issues, or evaluating competing research hypotheses—Sciorex offers a Council Mode in which multiple AI models engage in a structured, round-based discussion. Each participant can be configured with a custom council persona—a reusable profile with its own system prompt, temperature setting, and role description. Personas can be created manually, imported from the community marketplace, or exported as YAML files for sharing with collaborators. The researcher poses a question and observes as different models reason through the problem from their configured perspectives, often surfacing insights that a single model would miss. Beyond councils, Agent Teams enable multi-agent collaboration where specialized agents work together on complex tasks, each contributing domain-specific expertise—for instance, a “Literature Reviewer” agent gathering sources while a “LaTeX Writer” agent drafts sections and a “Code Analyst” validates experimental results. This adversarial-collaborative approach mirrors the peer review and research team dynamics that researchers are already familiar with.

agents.title: Custom Agents
agents.p1: Researchers can define reusable AI agents with specialized system prompts, tool permissions, and input/output schemas. A “Research Orchestrator” agent might be configured to clarify research goals, create tickets, manage the library, and coordinate experiments—while a “Code Reviewer” agent focuses solely on code quality. Agents can be created manually, generated by an AI assistant, or imported from the community marketplace—which also hosts shared workflows, council personas, and LaTeX templates. Each agent runs in a sandboxed local environment with configurable permission levels (from fully autonomous to requiring approval for every action).

agentExecution.title: Agent Execution & History
agentExecution.p1: Every agent execution is recorded with full message history, tool calls, and output. Researchers can review what an agent did, inspect individual tool invocations, and continue conversations from any point. Multiple agents can run in parallel across different worktrees, enabling side-by-side comparison of different approaches to the same problem.

workflows.title: Visual Workflows
workflows.p1: Complex research pipelines—data preprocessing, model training, figure generation, paper compilation—often involve dozens of interdependent steps. Sciorex provides a visual, node-based workflow editor where users can compose automation pipelines by connecting pre-built and custom nodes. The node palette includes triggers, AI agent nodes, conditional branching, parallel execution, wait checkpoints (for human approval), data transforms, and ticket actions. Workflows support real-time debugging with breakpoints, step-through execution, and per-node output inspection.

flowMonitoring.title: Flow Execution Monitoring
flowMonitoring.p1: Running workflows are monitored in real time. The execution view visualizes node-by-node progress, highlights the currently executing node, and provides interactive decision panels for error handling and loop control. Completed runs are logged with full execution traces, making research pipelines auditable and reproducible.

editor.title: Integrated Editor
editor.p1: The built-in Monaco-based editor supports syntax highlighting for all major languages, VIM mode, multi-tab editing, a file tree browser with multi-select and drag-and-drop operations, and a code outline panel. Beyond standard code files, it handles Markdown with preview, Jupyter notebooks, PDFs, images, HTML preview, LaTeX documents, a rich-text editor (TipTap) for note-taking, and a 3D molecule viewer for structural biology files. On Linux and macOS, an embedded VS Code Server provides a full VS Code environment alongside the primary editor; on Windows, the same capability is available via VS Code CLI serve-web. A live browser preview panel with Playwright CDP synchronization enables side-by-side frontend development: Sciorex auto-detects running dev servers, and the AI can interact with the live browser directly. The agentic preview mode shows AI-generated diffs for review before applying changes. A built-in process explorer with memory tracking gives researchers full visibility into running background tasks.

sourceControl.title: Source Control & Worktrees
sourceControl.p1: Git is a free version-control system widely used in both software engineering and computational research. It tracks every change to your files, lets you revert to earlier versions, and makes it simple to back up your work to free hosting services like GitHub or GitLab. When Git is installed on your system, Sciorex provides a visual interface for it: a diff viewer, commit graph, branch management, and staged/unstaged change tracking—no command line needed. Projects are plain folders; initialize Git whenever you want version control.
sourceControl.p2: For researchers working on multiple experiments simultaneously, Git worktree support allows parallel branch workspaces—each with its own independent working directory and AI sessions. Worktree merging with built-in conflict detection makes it straightforward to reconcile divergent experiments. This enables a workflow where one worktree runs an experiment while another explores an alternative approach, with results compared side by side before merging the winning approach back into the main branch.

mcp.title: AI Autonomy & the MCP Layer
mcp.p1: What distinguishes Sciorex from a collection of colocated tools is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) layer {{cite5}} that binds them together. MCP exposes 59 custom tools (and counting) across multiple specialized servers, giving AI models direct access to every subsystem in the application. Researchers can also register their own MCP-compatible servers in the workspace configuration, extending the AI’s capabilities to any external tool or service that implements the protocol. This transforms the AI from a text-based assistant into an autonomous research collaborator that can operate across the full spectrum of research activities.
mcp.p2: The following is a representative subset of the MCP capabilities, organized by domain. Each tool can be invoked by any AI model during a chat session, subject to the researcher’s permission settings.

tools: pdf_read — Extract text from PDFs by page range
pdf_annotate — Add highlights, underlines, comments
pdf_get_annotations — Retrieve all annotations from a PDF
latex_compile — Compile LaTeX (pdflatex/xelatex/lualatex)
library_add_item — Add papers, books, datasets to library
library_manage — Create/update collections and tags
library_search — Search papers via Semantic Scholar, arXiv, CrossRef
sciorex_create_ticket — Create tickets with type, priority, subtasks
sciorex_change_status — Move tickets through workflow stages
sciorex_report_progress — Report completion % and milestones
sciorex_create_epic — Group tickets into milestone epics
sciorex_link_resource — Link papers, branches, sessions to tickets
sciorex_add_comment — Add comments and discussion threads
sciorex_save_agent — Create or update custom AI agents
sciorex_save_flow — Create or update automation workflows
sciorex_execute_agent — Launch agent execution in background
sciorex_execute_flow — Trigger flow execution with parameters
sciorex_list_agents — Browse available agents and templates
sciorex_ask_user — Ask questions with single/multi-select options
sciorex_request_approval — Request explicit user approval
sciorex_notify_user — Send info/warning/error notifications
sciorex_set_view_mode — Switch between chat, agentic, and preview
request_secret — Securely access secrets (value never exposed to AI)
release_secret — Release granted secrets when no longer needed
add_secret — Store new secrets with user confirmation
list_secrets — List available secret names (values never shown)

mcp.permissions: The permission system provides three levels of AI autonomy: a “YOLO” mode where the AI operates freely, an “auto-approve edits” mode where file changes are applied automatically but other actions require confirmation, and an “ask for all” mode where every tool invocation requires explicit researcher approval. This graduated control allows researchers to calibrate trust as they become familiar with the system’s capabilities.
mcp.practical: The practical implication is that a researcher can instruct the AI to “download the latest paper on transformer architectures, add it to my reference library, annotate the key findings, and create a ticket to review its methodology”—and the AI can execute this entire workflow autonomously, using the MCP tools to interact with the PDF viewer, library, and ticket system without any manual intervention.

project.title: Project Management
project.p1: Research projects benefit from structured task tracking, especially in collaborative settings. Sciorex includes a built-in project management system with Kanban boards, a ticket list view, and epics for organizing work across longer timelines. Unlike external project management tools, Sciorex’s system is tightly coupled with the codebase and research documents: tickets can be linked to specific files, Git branches, AI sessions, flow runs, and library papers. AI models can create, update, and query tickets through MCP, enabling automated progress tracking where the AI reports completion percentages and milestones as it works.
project.p2: For larger research endeavors—thesis chapters, multi-paper projects, or grant deliverables—Epics provide a higher-level organizational layer. Epics group related tickets into coherent milestones, offering progress tracking across the entire scope of a research project. This hierarchical structure scales from a single-author study to multi-team collaborative efforts.

architecture.title: Architecture & Privacy
architecture.p1: Sciorex is built on a local-first architecture. The application runs entirely on the user’s desktop with no mandatory cloud services, no user accounts, and no telemetry. All data—projects, references, annotations, AI conversation history, workflow definitions—is stored on the local filesystem in open, human-readable formats wherever possible. Projects are plain folders that can be git-initialized at any time, giving researchers free backup to GitHub, GitLab, or any Git remote—without depending on any proprietary sync service.
architecture.p2: This design is a deliberate response to the growing trend of cloud-dependent research tools that create data lock-in and raise legitimate concerns about intellectual property exposure. Since Sciorex wraps external AI CLIs, all communication goes directly from the CLI to its model provider—Sciorex itself never relays, intercepts, or stores any data. It does not operate relay servers, does not collect usage data, and does not require an internet connection for any core functionality beyond the CLI’s own model access and literature search. For researchers requiring complete offline operation, Sciorex supports local CLIs: LM Studio and Ollama.
architecture.p3: The secrets management system ensures that tokens and credentials are stored securely and never exposed to AI models—when a CLI requests access to a secret, it receives only an environment variable reference, with the actual value injected securely at execution time.

privacyGuarantee.heading: Privacy guarantee:
privacyGuarantee.line1: All data remains on the user’s machine.
privacyGuarantee.line2: No cloud dependency. No telemetry. No data collection.
privacyGuarantee.line3: Secrets never exposed to AI models.

availability.title: Availability
availability.p1: Sciorex is freely available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. The application is distributed as native installers for each platform and requires no account creation or license key.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.p1: Sciorex Personal is free and includes all features described in this paper. There are no feature gates, no trial limitations, and no premium tiers that restrict core functionality. If your institution requires team workspaces, collaboration, or enterprise features, contact us to discuss upcoming plans.

items.a: Yes. Completely free for personal and professional use—no subscriptions, no premium tiers, no hidden costs. Sciorex works by wrapping AI CLIs (command-line interfaces)—small programs like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Ollama that you install separately on your computer. Sciorex provides the graphical interface and orchestration on top. Your costs are whatever the CLI charges, or zero with fully local models via LM Studio or Ollama.

items.q: Can AI models actually annotate my PDFs and manage my library?
items.a: Yes. Through the MCP protocol, AI models can read PDF content (pdf_read), add highlights and comments (pdf_annotate), retrieve existing annotations (pdf_get_annotations), add papers to your reference library (library_add_item), manage collections and tags (library_manage), and attach notes (library_add_note)—all autonomously during a chat session. You can ask the AI to “read this paper, highlight the methodology section, and add it to my literature review collection” and it will execute each step using the appropriate tools.

Over 30 publication-ready templates: NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ACL, EMNLP, AAAI, IJCAI, IEEE (conference and journal), ACM (SIGCHI, SIGPLAN, etc.), Nature, Science, Springer (LNCS), Elsevier, APS (Physical Review), PNAS, PhD Thesis, Master’s Thesis, and general article formats. Each template includes the correct bibliography style and can be compiled with pdflatex, xelatex, or lualatex.

items.q: How does the reference library compare to Zotero or Mendeley?
items.a: Sciorex’s library supports 43 item types, 11 citation styles (APA, MLA, IEEE, Chicago, Harvard, Vancouver, Nature, Science, ACM, APS, and custom CSL), and imports/exports in BibTeX, RIS, CSL-JSON, Zotero, and Mendeley formats. The key difference is AI integration: your language models can search for papers, add them to collections, generate citations, and insert references into LaTeX documents—something traditional reference managers cannot do. All data is stored locally on your machine.

items.q: Can I use Sciorex completely offline?
items.a: Yes. Install a local AI CLI like LM Studio or Ollama (both free), and Sciorex operates entirely offline with no internet connection required. Paper discovery (Semantic Scholar, arXiv, CrossRef, PubMed, and other online sources) naturally requires internet, but all other features—the editor, LaTeX compilation, PDF annotation, library management, ticket tracking, and workflows—work fully offline.

items.q: Where is my data stored? Is my research private?
items.a: Everything stays on your local filesystem—100% of it. Sciorex collects no analytics, no telemetry, and no usage data. Your papers, annotations, library, conversations, and code never leave your machine. Projects are plain folders—if you install Git (a free version-control tool), you can track changes and back up your work to GitHub or GitLab at no cost. Secrets (tokens, credentials) are stored in an encrypted local vault and never exposed to AI models. The only network traffic is between the CLI and its provider when you initiate a chat.

items.q: What is MCP and why should researchers care?
items.a: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that gives AI models the ability to use tools—not just generate text, but actually perform actions. In practice, this means you can tell the AI “read this paper, highlight the methodology section, add it to my literature review collection, and create a ticket to follow up” and it will do each step autonomously. Sciorex exposes 59 custom tools (and counting) across multiple servers covering PDFs, the reference library, project tickets, workflows, interactions, and secrets. You can also register your own MCP-compatible servers to extend the AI’s capabilities further. It transforms AI from a chatbot into a research assistant that can operate across your entire workspace.

items.q: How is Sciorex different from Cursor, Windsurf, or Overleaf?
items.a: Sciorex is neither a code editor nor an online LaTeX editor—it’s a complete research environment. Unlike Cursor or Windsurf (code-focused IDEs), Sciorex includes PDF annotation, a reference library, paper discovery, LaTeX with 30+ templates, project management with kanban boards, a 3D molecule viewer, and an embedded VS Code Server. Unlike Overleaf (cloud LaTeX), Sciorex runs 100% locally, supports AI-assisted writing with any model, and integrates code editing alongside document preparation. Council Mode lets multiple AI models debate problems, with custom personas you can tailor or import from the community marketplace. It wraps existing AI CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) so you keep full control.

items.q: Do I need programming experience to use Sciorex?
items.a: No. While Sciorex includes a powerful code editor and agent framework, many researchers use it primarily for PDF reading, literature management, LaTeX writing, and AI-assisted research tasks—none of which require programming. The visual workflow builder uses drag-and-drop, and the AI chat interface accepts natural language instructions. Researchers who do write code (Python, R, MATLAB) benefit from the integrated development environment.
